Based on the CD18 expression on neutrophils, LAD1 was sub-classified into three phenotypes viz. severe (LAD1°) with CD18 expression <2% moderate (LAD1^-) phenotype with CD18 expression 2%–30%, and mild (LAD1^+) phenotype with CD18 expression ≥30%.
Molecular confirmation was performed was done using Sanger sequencing for LAD1 and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for LAD3.

authors_classification.statement: Cohort-level only: the authors call the 57 ITGB2 variants of Table S2 'disease-causing' and say 35 were novel. No per-variant classification or ACMG criteria. Table S2's references column for this variant reads 'MT488441'.

quotes.quote: Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients (Table S2), including 30 patients we have previously reported (18).

concerns: Single source: a multicentre retrospective cohort (Kambli 2020, PMID 33391282); per-person genotypes come only from Supplementary Table S2, which gives no transcript and no genomic coordinates.
The paper says 30 of its patients were reported before in its ref 18 (Madkaikar 2015, PMID 25703682) without naming them, so carriers here may be the same people as in that paper.

Table S2's '#' marks are inconsistent: P23, P63 and P76 carry one '#'-marked and one unmarked variant, 12 patients are '#'-marked in all, while the text says compound heterozygous variants were found in only 10 patients.
No parental or family testing is described for LAD1 (the family-testing sentence in the methods refers to NGS for LAD3); Table S1 has a Family History column but no genotyped relatives.
P72 also carries c.751G>A (p.Gly251Ser), candidate G-lad1-048 (same person, LAD1-ID0185).
notes_for_panel: All evidence comes from one multicentre Indian cohort (PMID 33391282): genotypes from Supplementary Table S2, clinical rows from Supplementary Table S1. No segregation, de novo, phase or variant-level functional data are reported; the CD18 flow-cytometry subtype is the only per-person laboratory finding. Zygosity is per-person only through Table S2's '#' marks, which are inconsistent.
